notes.meaning: God announces judgment against the leaders of Judah for failing to care for His people. In the ancient world, kings and rulers were often called shepherds. Instead of protecting the people like sheep in a good pasture, these rulers mistreated them and drove them toward ruin. Leaders are responsible to God for how they treat the people in their care.

The Lord directly confronts the royal shepherds who were supposed to feed and guide Israel. Because they ignored and scattered the flock, God says He will now pay attention to them in judgment. The word for caring for sheep is the same word used for calling someone to account. God never overlooks the harm done by selfish leaders.

God promises that He Himself will step in and gather the survivors of His flock from the lands of exile. Even though foreign armies carried the people away, God had allowed it as a discipline. He plans to bring them back home, where they will flourish and grow in safety once again. God's mercy always follows His judgment.

differ.view: This global gathering looks beyond the return from Babylon to a final physical return of the Jewish people to their land in the end times.
The promise began in the return from Babylon and finds its main fulfillment as Christ gathers His elect people from all nations into the church.

notes.meaning: The Lord promises to place faithful leaders over His people who will genuinely tend and nurture them. Under these good shepherds, the people will not live in terror or constant worry, and not a single sheep will be left behind or lost. God's ideal for leadership is safety, peace, and personal care for every individual.

God points to a coming King from King David's family line, calling Him a righteous Branch or green shoot. Even though David's royal line seemed cut down like a dead tree, new life would sprout from it. This King will rule wisely and govern the land with complete fairness and justice. Christians see this as a promise of Jesus the Messiah.

During the reign of this King, both Judah and Israel will live together in safety and freedom from enemies. He will be called 'The LORD Our Righteousness,' showing that He gives His people a right standing before God. The name also stands in sharp contrast to King Zedekiah, whose name meant 'the Lord is righteous' but whose reign was corrupt. True security comes from resting in God's righteousness rather than human strength.

differ.view: The title shows that Christ gives His own perfect obedience to believers, counting them fully righteous in God's sight.
The title proves Christ's divine nature and shows that He justifies believers and empowers them to live truly holy lives.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Jeremiah likely meant that under this ideal Davidic king, God would ensure social justice and right living throughout the nation, rather than describing a doctrine of personal salvation.

notes.meaning: A day is coming when God's people will no longer swear by the ancient rescue from Egypt. Instead, they will praise the Lord for bringing them back from the northern land of Babylon and all other places of exile. This future rescue will be so great that it will overshadow the wonders of the Exodus. God's new acts of grace give His people fresh reasons to praise Him.

Jeremiah begins a new section confronting the false prophets, and the thought of their sin leaves him heartbroken. His body trembles and he feels dizzy, like a drunken man overcome by wine. He is overwhelmed because he sees the vast gap between God's holy words and the wickedness of these religious leaders. Standing in the presence of God's holiness makes human sin feel unbearable.

The land is filled with people being unfaithful to God, practicing both physical adultery and idol worship. Because of God's curse against their covenant-breaking, the land is suffering a severe drought and the green pastures have dried up. The leaders use their strength and authority for evil rather than good. When leaders chase wickedness, whole communities suffer the fallout.

Both the prophets and the priests have become thoroughly corrupt and ungodly. The Lord declares that He has uncovered their wicked deeds inside His own temple. The very men who were called to teach God's law and offer holy sacrifices brought their sin into the most sacred place. Religious titles mean nothing if our hearts are far from God.

God warns that the path these leaders walk will become slick and dark, making them slip and fall. They think they are walking safely, but disaster will overtake them when God's set time of punishment arrives. Sin blinds people to danger until it is too late to turn back. God always sets a limit on unrepentant wickedness.

The Lord reminds Judah of what happened long ago among the prophets of Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom. Those prophets openly served the false god Baal and led the people of Israel far astray into idol worship. Their foolish idolatry eventually brought the destruction of their nation. Past warnings from history should keep us from making the same mistakes.

The prophets in Jerusalem are even worse than the Baal prophets of the north, because they claim to speak for the Lord while living in adultery and deceit. Instead of rebuking sin, they encourage evildoers and make them feel comfortable in their wickedness. God says Jerusalem has become like the wicked ancient cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to Him. The worst kind of deception is using God's name to justify sinful living.

The Lord of Hosts announces that He will feed these corrupt prophets bitter wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink. Because the spiritual leaders of Jerusalem spread godlessness across the entire land, their punishment will be exceptionally bitter. Leaders who poison others with false teaching will taste God's severe judgment. Great responsibility brings great accountability.

God commands the people not to pay attention to the messages of these popular prophets. These teachers fill their listeners with false hopes, inventing visions out of their own imaginations rather than speaking from God's mouth. They tell people what they want to hear instead of what God has actually spoken. We must test every message against God's revealed truth.

The false prophets keep telling people who despise God that they will enjoy peace and prosperity. They tell stubborn rebels that no harm will ever touch them. This soothed the people into a false sense of security while judgment was at the door. Promising peace to those who refuse to repent is the clear mark of a false teacher.

The Lord asks which of these flattering prophets has ever stood in His heavenly council to hear His secret plans. None of them had paid attention to God's voice or obeyed what He commanded. A person cannot speak faithfully for God without first listening closely to Him. True spiritual authority comes only from being in God's presence.

Instead of the peace that the false prophets promised, the Lord's anger is like a furious storm breaking loose. His judgment will whirl down like a destructive tornado upon the heads of the wicked. No human lie can calm the storm of divine justice when it begins to blow. God's warnings are real and should never be taken lightly.

God's anger will not back down until He has accomplished everything He planned. In days to come, especially after the coming exile, the people will finally look back and understand what happened with perfect clarity. God's plans are steady and sure, even when people refuse to believe them. One day every doubt about God's word will be cleared away.

The Lord declares that He never sent these prophets, yet they rushed out eagerly to preach on their own. He never gave them a message, yet they pretended to prophesy in His name. Being enthusiastic about speaking in church or public is not enough without a true call from God. God values obedience and truth far above human ambition.

If these men had truly stood in God's council, their message would have produced real spiritual fruit. They would have preached God's holy word and urged the people to turn away from their evil deeds. The clearest test of true ministry is whether it leads people away from sin and toward God. Words that encourage sin never come from heaven.

The Lord asks whether He is merely a local god close by and not also a God far away. The false prophets treated Him like a small neighborhood idol who could only see what was right in front of Him. God is not confined to one place or limited in His awareness. God's rule and sight extend over every corner of existence.

God asks if anyone can really hide in secret places where He cannot see them. He declares that His presence fills the entire universe, both heaven and earth. Nothing can be hidden from His sight, no matter how private people think their actions are. Living with an awareness of God's presence keeps us honest and humble.

God states that He has heard every word spoken by these dishonest prophets. They claimed with great excitement that they had received special dreams from God, but they were telling lies in His name. Using religious language to cover up personal opinions is deeply offensive to the Lord. God hears and evaluates every claim people make about Him.

The Lord asks how long these prophets will keep making up lies from the deceit of their own minds. Their false messages were not simple mistakes; they came from deliberate planning in their own hearts. God patiently challenges them to stop poisoning the minds of the people. God sees the motives behind every word spoken in His name.

These prophets intended to make the people forget God's true character by trading their made-up dreams back and forth. Their influence was having the exact same effect as the ancient worship of Baal, which had caused earlier generations to abandon God. Replacing God's truth with human fantasies always leads people away from Him. We must guard our hearts against anything that crowds out God's true character.

God gives a simple rule: let someone who has an ordinary dream tell it as a dream, but let the one who has God's word speak it faithfully. He asks what dry straw has in common with nourishing wheat. Human ideas are empty and useless like straw, while God's word feeds and sustains spiritual life like grain. We should never trade the life-giving truth of scripture for human opinions.

The Lord compares His word to a blazing fire and to a heavy hammer that shatters solid rock. Fire burns away the dry straw of human falsehood, and a hammer breaks down the hardest, most stubborn hearts. God's message has real, supernatural power to change people and tear down self-righteous pride. No human stubbornness is too hard for God's word to break through.

The Lord declares that He stands against the prophets who steal His words from one another. Instead of hearing directly from God, they borrowed phrases and ideas from true prophets and from each other, twisting them to fit their own agendas. Mimicking spiritual language does not make someone a messenger from heaven. God looks for genuine truthfulness, not borrowed catchphrases.

God again warns that He is against those who simply wag their own tongues and claim, 'The LORD declares it.' They spoke with smooth words and acted like authoritative messengers, but they were only voicing their own thoughts. Tacking God's name onto human ideas is a serious misuse of His authority. True messengers speak only what God has given them to say.

God confirms that He is against those who spread reckless lies based on false dreams, leading the people into dangerous error. Because God never sent them or gave them a command, their teachings bring no help or benefit to the people at all. False teaching always leaves souls empty and spiritually bankrupt. God's genuine guidance is the only thing that truly helps us.

When the people or their leaders mockingly ask Jeremiah, 'What is the burden of the LORD?', he is told to turn their question back on them. In Hebrew, the word for a prophetic message also meant a heavy load, and they were sneering at Jeremiah's warnings. God replies that they themselves are the tiresome burden, and He plans to throw them off. Mocking God's warnings only speeds up His judgment.

God warns that anyone who flippantly uses the phrase 'the burden of the LORD' will face divine punishment along with their whole family. The people had turned a sacred phrase into a disrespectful joke to mock God's serious messages. Treating holy things with careless contempt brings grave danger. God expects His words to be treated with reverent care.

The Lord tells the people how they should talk to each other instead of making disrespectful jokes. When asking a neighbor or friend about God's will, they should simply ask, 'What has the LORD answered?' or 'What has the LORD spoken?' God wants everyday conversations about spiritual matters to be respectful and sincere. The words we use to speak of God reflect the state of our hearts.

The people are forbidden to use the word 'burden' to describe God's messages any longer. If they keep calling His words a burden, their own careless talk will become a heavy weight of guilt crushing them down. Mocking God's revelation perverts the word of the living God and turns what should be a blessing into judgment. We must never resent the corrections of God's word.

When anyone approaches a true prophet, they are told to ask with simple respect, 'What has the LORD answered you?' or 'What has the LORD spoken?' God repeats this instruction to drive home the need for humble language when seeking His guidance. Approaching God's servants with reverence opens the way to receive His truth. A teachable attitude prepares us to hear God's voice.

The Lord explains what will happen if people stubbornly keep using the forbidden mocking phrase after being warned. Continuing to say 'the burden of the LORD' proves that they are deliberately defying God's clear command. Knowing what God forbids and doing it anyway leaves a person without any excuse. God takes intentional defiance very seriously.

Because of their persistent mockery, God promises to pick them up like a heavy load and cast them completely out of His presence. Both the people and the holy city of Jerusalem will be discarded in judgment. God will bring an enduring shame and disgrace upon them that history will never forget, which was fulfilled in their defeat and exile to Babylon. Those who proudly reject God's word ultimately lose everything they took pride in.
